assessments.reasoning: The specification at 6851–6879 places ordinary evaluation of the function value and call arguments in the caller and the subsequent invocation in the new goroutine. The referenced Calls rule at 4194–4229 makes argument evaluation anterior to invocation and provides the runtime-panic case for a nil function value. The official Go release tag resolves to the pinned commit and the independently retrieved bytes match the registered digest.

challenge.method: Trace a call with side-effecting argument evaluation. Challenge the inference that starting a new goroutine transfers argument evaluation, orders the rest of the caller after the callee, or makes a nil callee run its body.
challenge.results: Function-value and argument evaluation belong to the original goroutine before invocation proceeds in the new goroutine. The caller's later instructions and callee have independent execution. The ordering rule also permits a nil function value to panic at invocation after argument evaluation.

limitations: The rule orders evaluation and invocation. A nil callee can panic at the call boundary without running a body. Scheduling after the statement and operating-system thread mapping are outside this rule.
